statements.text: I want to talk to you about surveillance and the Internet of Things. As you know, the PRC is exporting facial recognition AI technology, enabling repression from Ecuador to Kenya to Pakistan.
statements.context: Senate hearing on U.S. strategic competition with the PRC, featuring Senator Schatz questioning a witness on surveillance technology exports.

statements.text: I do think it is unclear to me what we are doing instead of the AI Safety Institute, and we have got to work on a bipartisan basis to figure out what takes its place.
statements.context: Senate confirmation hearing for Howard Lutnick as Secretary of Commerce.

statements.text: President Trump rolled back the Biden EO on the AI Safety Institute.
statements.context: Senate confirmation hearing for Howard Lutnick as Commerce Secretary.

statements.text: It seems to me that on the consumer side that one of the most basic rights of a user on the Internet is to understand what they are looking at or listening to and whether or not it was created solely by a person, a person using an AI, or automatically generated using AI. Do you think a labeling regime—not a prohibition on the use of AI but just the disclosure, especially as it relates to images, music, creativity—do you think a label would be helpful for consumers?
statements.context: Senate hearing on strengthening U.S. computing and AI capabilities, where Senator Schatz questions a witness about AI policy and consumer protections.

statements.text: For the government actually delivering services I want you to describe what an AI agent or AI can do to kind of reduce those pain points that we accept as a fact of life in interacting with the government. It seems to me so much of what makes us irritated with the government is the lack of sorting data that exists somewhere but we cannot get access to it.
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'Winning the AI Race: Strengthening U.S. Capabilities in Computing and Innovation,' featuring testimony from industry executives including Sam Altman and Brad Smith.
